record.original_question: Prove global existence and uniqueness for initial-boundary value problems in properly formulated dynamic theories of nonlinear elasticity, including isothermal thermoelastic or thermoviscoelastic equations with appropriate boundary and initial data.

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Prove the global existence and uniqueness of solutions to initialboundary value problems for properly formulated dynamic theories of nonlinear elasticity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain occupied (in a reference configuration) by a hyperelastic body, and let $\varphi : \Omega \times [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the deformation, with deformation gradient $F = \nabla \varphi$ required to satisfy $\det F > 0$. Assume a stored-energy function $W : M^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ that is frame-indifferent and polyconvex (or, more generally, satisfies standard constitutive hypotheses of nonlinear elasticity, including $W(F) \to \infty$ as $\det F \to 0^+$), and let the first Piola–Kirchhoff stress be $S(F) = \partial W / \partial F$.

Consider the equations of motion of nonlinear elastodynamics
$$\rho_0\, \varphi_{tt} = \operatorname{div} S(\nabla \varphi) + b \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,\infty),$$
where $\rho_0 > 0$ is the reference mass density and $b$ is a given body force, supplemented by mixed boundary conditions
$$\varphi = \varphi_0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega_D \times (0,\infty), \qquad S(\nabla\varphi)\, n = t_N \text{ on } \partial\Omega_N \times (0,\infty),$$
with $\partial\Omega = \overline{\partial\Omega_D} \cup \overline{\partial\Omega_N}$, and initial data
$$\varphi(\cdot,0) = \varphi_0, \qquad \varphi_t(\cdot,0) = v_0.$$
One may equally consider the corresponding isothermal thermoelastic or thermoviscoelastic systems obtained by coupling the above with the balance of energy and a constitutive law for the heat flux, supplemented by appropriate thermal boundary and initial conditions.

Problem. For a suitably formulated such initial–boundary value problem, prove the global existence and uniqueness of a solution (in an appropriate weak or measure-valued sense compatible with the constitutive assumptions and ensuring $\det \nabla \varphi > 0$ a.e. for all $t > 0$), for arbitrary smooth initial data of finite energy.
artifact.status_search_result: Global existence and uniqueness for the initial–boundary value problem of three-dimensional nonlinear elastodynamics (and its thermo(visco)elastic counterparts) is widely regarded as a major open problem. Only local-in-time existence, small-data global existence (e.g. results of Sideris and others for the Cauchy problem in unbounded domains with null conditions), and special one-dimensional or viscoelastic regularized cases are known. No general global well-posedness theorem in the polyconvex finite-elasticity setting is available.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in elasticity (J. M. Ball)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 12. Prove the global existence and uniqueness of solutions to initial-boundary value problems for properly formulated dynamic theories of nonlinear elasticity.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open problem in nonlinear elastodynamics.

status_evidence.title: Sideris, Global existence of small-amplitude solutions in nonlinear elastodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence is established for small-data Cauchy problems under null conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Only small-data/Cauchy results are known; general global well-posedness remains open.
